classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the diagonal forms a right triangle with two equal unknown legs, solve twice the side square, then convert the exact side length to perimeter before rounding.

content.prompt: Find the perimeter of a square with diagonal length $6\text{ cm}$. Keep intermediate values exact and use a calculator in the final step. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let the side length be $s$ cm. The diagonal divides the square into two right-angled triangles with equal shorter sides.

$$\begin{align*}s^2+s^2&=6^2\\2s^2&=36\\s^2&=18\\s&=\sqrt{18}\end{align*}$$

Keeping the side length exact until the final step,

$$\begin{align*}P&=4\sqrt{18}\text{ cm}\\P&\approx16.97\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
